neighbours.label: Removal of something from where it belongs: ' away'/' out' right after a verb of taking or carrying (taken away, carried out of, moved out); weaker on ' remove'. The - pole is the other side: letting go (release, spit out, dropped)
fire: During the night the soldiers took the paintings away from the palace in trucks.
After the inspection the damaged crates were taken away and stored in a shed.
Social workers decided that the two boys should be taken out of the foster home.
Before the flood reached the library, volunteers carried the oldest books out of the basement.
When the factory closed, the machines were hauled away and sold for scrap.
The museum had the statue taken away from the square for cleaning.
Each evening the stale bread is moved out of the shop and given to farmers.
The police led the prisoner away from the courtroom through a side door.
quiet: During the night the soldiers figured out where the paintings had been hidden.
After the inspection the damaged crates turned out to be empty.
Social workers pointed out that the two boys were happy in the foster home.
The village is far away from the library, so volunteers bring books by van.
When the factory closed, the workers found out from a notice on the gate.
The museum stands a mile away from the square where the statue is.
Each evening the baker lets the stray dog go after feeding it by the door.
The police set the prisoner free and he walked into the courtroom to thank them.

notes: Card: ' out' x8, ' away' x6, remove/removing/removal after take/move verbs; the - pole peaks on release, spit out, let go. Probes: 'took the children away' 0.54, 'carried out of the building' 0.37, 'remove the tumor' 0.12, 'found out the truth' 0.01, 'flew off' 0.04.
